title: E03 revision-bound knowledge: does a run notice that a fact it read has gone stale?
hypothesis: Both arms can re-read a mutated file, so the question is not whether staleness is survivable but what it costs. With `ctx.taskstate.v1` the projection drops facts whose file revision is no longer current, so the run should touch the mutated file more often and pass at least as often; the legacy profile keeps the stale text and should pass less often without saving work.
disclosure: A smoke run of the legacy arm (1 repetition, both tasks, both passed, 178 100 and 104 854 tokens) preceded this file because the harness itself needed to be proven end to end; it is excluded from every number below. The suite and the harness were frozen before that smoke run, only the preregistration was late.

task_cluster_definition.cluster: one task is one cluster; each task rewrites the file it told the agent to read, twice, mid-run
task_cluster_definition.dev_suite_note: unrelated static suite; not used here
task_cluster_definition.revision_plan: each task rewrites its config module at t=25 s and again at t=55 s; the graded contract is the post-revision state
task_cluster_definition.fairness_check: each task graded unsolved (exit 1) and with a reference solution (exit 0) after the final revision, before any run
task_cluster_definition.harness: scripts/run-revision-experiment.py - runs kroma directly, applies the revisions on a timer, then grades with the out-of-workspace verifier

model_identity_observability.note: same model both arms; absolute token claims carry the model identity

quality_margin.rule: quality non-inferior within 5pp before any cost claim

noise_and_power_plan.plan: 8 runs; same model, fixed revision offsets, arm order alternated
noise_and_power_plan.statement: 2 clusters cannot establish a distribution; the report states direction and whether the interval crosses zero, and nothing stronger

cache_order_design.cache: provider-side cache state is not controllable and is not claimed

stopping_rule: stop after 8 runs or 3 000k tokens, whichever comes first

holdout_policy.retirement_action: this suite becomes validation; a new one must be frozen before another claim
